A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Chain-of-Memory research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained and added content.

before.justification: v1 reports original LongMemEval and LoCoMo experiments, including accuracy and computational costs, component ablations, hyperparameter tests, and error analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds reranking comparisons, gating ablations, truncation-threshold sensitivity, and embedding-model robustness experiments.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 retain turn-level memory nodes, top-K retrieval, top-L anchors, multiplicative gating, and adaptive truncation through unchanged Equations 1–4. Newly documented candidate removal and reuse in Section 3.3 do not establish a procedural revision.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate LongMemEval-S and LoCoMo with the same four question categories and exclusion of LoCoMo adversarial questions. The added experiments reuse this dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix A.2 adds an evaluated bge-reranker-base cross-encoder baseline on both datasets with both LLM backbones, reported in Tables 6–7. Original comparators remain. Iterative retrieval is discussed but has no reported experimental comparison.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark splits, metrics, backbones, and retrieval settings remain. Added experiments introduce three alternative gating controls, a beta sweep over 0.3, 0.5, and 0.7, replacement with text-embedding-3-small, and expanded-candidate-pool reranking.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablation, retrieval-size sweep, upper-bound comparison, and error analysis, v2 adds gating-formulation ablations, truncation-threshold sensitivity, and robustness across embedding models. Tables 3–4 and 8–9 substantially broaden investigation of the method's design choices and dependencies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, variability estimates, or significance tests. The added results continue to use point estimates without uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 3–4 and 6–9 add substantial results for gating, thresholds, reranking, and alternate embeddings. For example, with text-embedding-3-small and Qwen3-32B, CoM/RAG accuracy is 75.00/65.40 on LongMemEval and 70.12/65.06 on LoCoMo. These are additional settings; main Table 2 and the former Table 3, now Table 5, retain their results.

T1.justification: New Section 3.3 derives worst-case vector-similarity complexity O(LK^2d), and O(LTKd) when a maximum chain length T is imposed. v1 has no corresponding derivation. Existing mathematical definitions and method equations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the lightweight-construction/dynamic-utilization contribution and the same claimed accuracy and efficiency gains. The rewritten conclusion preserves the contribution's scientific meaning and scope.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the added tests as supporting chain organization beyond independent relevance scoring, a shared beta setting, and embedding robustness. Limitations newly emphasize weakly connected evidence and unvalidated interactive deployment with open-ended goals and noisy updates, while removing v1's assurance that modular retrieval mitigates embedding limitations.

D1.justification: v2 newly provides a code-repository link, identifies the reranker and its processing sequence, and clarifies within-chain candidate removal and cross-chain reuse. Appendix A.1 also adds a general judge-role instruction. These expand documentation without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: The reference list is unchanged. New Appendix A.2 explicitly positions CoM relative to reranking and iterative retrieval, distinguishing independent relevance scoring and query expansion from conditioning expansion on the evolving memory chain.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording corrections, revises affiliations, rewrites the conclusion and limitations, and adds acknowledgments. New analysis subsections and appendix sections extend the existing organization; most prior prose and section ordering remain.

P2.justification: New compact tables display gating, threshold, reranking, and embedding results. Existing figure designs and the overall layout remain, with localized changes including Figure 2 resizing and caption clarification, reformatted appendix prompt boxes, and relocation and renumbering of the upper-bound table.

improvement.justification: The added reranking control and targeted ablation and robustness tests strengthen support for the existing method. Complexity analysis, code-access information, and clearer deployment limitations improve transparency. The gains remain bounded by reporting gaps: new experiments still lack uncertainty estimates, and settings such as the reranker's expanded candidate-pool size remain unspecified.
